name: Dark Moody Painterly
description: Low-key painterly illustration in shadowy oil texture — desaturated charcoal, slate and umber with one restrained accent colour — contemplative, slightly unsettling, and calm in its composition.
style_bible: A dark, low-key painterly illustration worked in oil rather than rendered by a camera. Medium and surface: shadowy oil-paint texture throughout — thin scumbled darks that let a fine paint tooth show, softer blended passages where the light falls, and a little loaded paint only on the planes the light actually strikes. Edges stay soft in the shadow and firm where the single light meets a form. Nothing in the frame is glossy, plastic or photographic. Palette: desaturated charcoal, cold slate and warm umber, held close together in value, with exactly one restrained accent colour allowed to carry the eye — a dull crimson, a dim amber. There is no second accent and no saturated fill anywhere in the picture. Lighting: deep low-key light with soft pools of shadow. One source inside the frame, falling off quickly into darkness, so that a large part of the picture sits in the shadow range — but the midtones are kept open enough that silhouettes, hands and faces still read at small size instead of crushing to black. Composition: calm and quiet, with a strong focal subject, layered depth, and generous dark negative space around it and no clutter competing for the eye. The unease comes from what the darkness withholds, never from violence: nothing in the frame is wounded, bloody, monstrous or cruel. Keep the contract content-independent: no fixed subject, place, era, recurring motif or copied composition; the light and the restraint carry the style.
